title: Bolded advice-list items in self-help/how-to responses
description: This latent fires on individual bullet-point recommendations within listicle-style advice answers (often AI-generated), typically formatted as a short bolded label followed by a colon and elaboration (e.g. 'Network and build relationships**:', 'Set a budget**:', 'Look for error fares**:'). The pattern captures generic, actionable tips covering many topics -- career networking, gift-giving, travel deals, relationship advice, budgeting, self-care -- unified by their formulaic 'imperative phrase + explanation' structure as a discrete step in an enumerated list. It also extends to related list-item content like recommended websites/resources, follow-up clarifying questions posed to a user, and short reassuring/encouraging filler phrases that appear in the same advice-giving register. It does NOT include narrative prose, factual/explanatory statements without list formatting, dialogue transcripts unrelated to advice-giving, or purely descriptive sentences that lack the imperative 'tip' framing (e.g. scientific explanations, physical descriptions, or plain observations).

title: Validating and reassuring affirmation statements
description: This latent fires on formulaic, therapeutic-style reassurances that validate the reader's feelings, boundaries, autonomy, or worth, typically in advice-column or emotional-support contexts. Included sentences follow a recognizable template ('Remember, your X are valid/important, and you deserve/have the right to Y'), affirming that the addressee's emotions, needs, boundaries, or choices matter and licensing self-prioritization, self-advocacy, or seeking help ('you're not alone', 'it's okay to prioritize yourself'). It captures the rhetorical move of directly addressing 'you' with comforting, empowering validation rather than giving concrete advice, analysis, or describing a situation. Excluded are sentences that merely discuss relationships, compromise, or give practical/behavioral suggestions without this validating 'you deserve/it's okay' affirmation structure, as well as third-person or descriptive statements lacking direct emotional reassurance to the reader.

title: Advice-giving discourse scaffolding
description: This latent fires on the structural/rhetorical scaffolding of advice-oriented, self-help or interpersonal-guidance text rather than on any particular topic. It activates on discourse markers that introduce caveats or lists ('However,', 'It's also important to consider...', numbered/bolded list headers), imperative advice tips with bolded lead-in phrases ('Be specific**:', 'Pause before speaking**:'), and rapport-building or clarifying questions posed to a listener ('Could we discuss...?', 'Are you...?'). Included sentences are the connective tissue and formatting conventions of advice-giving prose -- transition words, bolded step/tip headers, softening qualifiers, and suggested dialogue/questions -- spanning topics from relationships to finance to games. It does NOT track the substantive content of the advice itself (e.g., specific facts about kidneys, dogs, or budgeting) or plain declarative statements lacking this list/transition/question scaffolding structure.

title: Empathetic conversational-assistant discourse markers
description: This latent fires on the stock phrases and structural scaffolding used by a chatbot-style assistant giving personal/relationship/advice-style responses in a warm, validating register: reassurances ('That's understandable,' 'That's great to hear!'), validation of the user's feelings or innocence ('You're not being unreasonable,' 'You are not the asshole'), empathetic transitions ('However,' 'Before I dive into my analysis, I want to acknowledge...'), list/enumeration scaffolding ('1. **', '2.', 'Here are some ideas:'), and rapport-building follow-up questions ('Would you like that?', 'What skills or resources...?'). Included are hedging disclaimers, soft transition connectives, numbered-list headers, and canned affective interjections ('That's frustrating!', 'I'm all ears!') that structure advice-giving or emotional-support text. Not included are sentences that merely discuss emotions, advice, or interpersonal topics in a neutral, third-person, or narrative way without this scaffolding/validating conversational function—i.e., the topic (dating, relationships, ethics, chores) is incidental; what matters is the assistant's rhetorical move of acknowledging, transitioning, listing, or reassuring.

title: Advice-column situation summarization
description: This latent fires on sentences in an advice/relationship-forum register that summarize, validate, or characterize the situation and behavior of the parties involved (you, a partner, family member, coworker, etc.) as part of a response to someone's personal dilemma. Included are statements that restate what happened ('Your friend chose a date that conflicts with your honeymoon'), evaluative judgments of behavior ('was quite harsh and dismissive', 'is a classic sign of emotional abuse'), and empathetic acknowledgments ('It's understandable that...', 'is concerning'), as well as bolded list-item headers introducing a factor or consideration ('Debt elimination:', 'Cultural sensitivity:'). It is not simply about any topic discussion or advice-giving generically—it specifically captures the narrative recap/assessment move of an advice-response, not direct instructions, questions, or neutral factual statements unrelated to characterizing someone's situation or conduct.

title: Empathetic advice-column stock phrases
description: This latent fires on the formulaic conversational scaffolding used in advice-giving/interpersonal-guidance responses (e.g., Reddit-relationship-advice or assistant chatbot style text): empathetic openers ('Wow, that's quite a story!', 'What a thoughtful gesture!', 'I'm so sorry to hear that...'), validating acknowledgments ('That's a valid concern', 'It's understandable that...'), and recommendation-style prompts ('Communicate your needs**:', 'Consider alternative solutions', 'Set boundaries**:'), often including numbered/bolded list-item stems and rhetorical framing phrases like 'The age-old conundrum of...' or 'Not necessarily.' The cluster includes short interjections, transitional validators, and templated advice-list headers that structure supportive or coaching-style dialogue, regardless of the underlying topic (gift cards, relationships, boundaries, finances, etc.). It does NOT include the substantive factual content or detailed reasoning that follows these openers/headers -- i.e., plain declarative facts, technical explanations, or narrative content without this empathetic/advisory framing are excluded, even if topically similar (e.g., a sentence merely stating a fact about HSV transmission without validating or advising language would not fit).

title: Empathetic validation in advice-giving
description: This latent fires on sentences from an advice-giving or interpersonal-conflict-mediation register (e.g., relationship/AITA-style responses), specifically the validating, empathizing, and evaluative moves a supportive advisor makes. Included are phrases that acknowledge and normalize the user's feelings ('It's completely understandable...', 'It sounds like...', 'That's a valid perspective'), that gently label another party's behavior as unacceptable or manipulative ('This is a classic manipulation tactic', 'not a constructive way to resolve the issue'), and that reframe the user's actions sympathetically ('You were just trying to...'). It also captures related empathetic openers, reflective questions, and reassurance-oriented framing ('completely normal', 'natural to feel'), including some second-person narrative recaps of a conflict situation used to set up such validation. It does NOT include purely factual/informational content, procedural instructions, or list items lacking this validating/empathizing stance (e.g., booking tips, identity-document requirements, or neutral factual claims), even when they appear in the same advice-column context—those are present only as low-activating background, not the core pattern.

title: Validating criticism while softening blame
description: This latent fires on sentences that perform a diplomatic 'yes, but' move in interpersonal advice or conflict contexts: acknowledging that a person's feelings, reaction, or complaint are valid or understandable, while simultaneously noting that the other party's approach, behavior, or effort was flawed or could have been better. It includes hedged evaluative statements like 'not unreasonable,' 'understandable that you'd feel X,' and 'your approach could have been more considerate,' as well as related soft critiques of specific behaviors (rushing a task, leaving the toilet seat up, being messy) framed as small failures of consideration. It excludes purely neutral factual statements, direct unhedged criticism without validation, and sentences that only state a question or fact (e.g., 'Your question, "Did you want it?"') without the accompanying empathetic-yet-critical framing that characterizes the rest of the cluster.

title: Reddit AITA-style reassurance framing
description: This latent fires on the stock conversational scaffolding used in Reddit advice-column responses, especially in r/AmItheAsshole-style contexts: formulaic openers ('Welcome to Reddit!', 'WIBTA?'), verdict-giving reassurances ('You're not the asshole here', 'You're not alone in feeling this way'), and validating meta-commentary that frames a situation before or after judging it ('The age-old conundrum of...', 'I think I know where you're going with this', 'It's great that you're being honest/self-aware'). Included sentences are short, templated, empathetic or judgment-framing phrases that a chatbot or forum responder uses as social lubricant around advice-giving, rather than substantive advice or object-level reasoning. Not included are sentences that give the actual content of the advice, factual claims, or detailed reasoning about the specific situation (e.g., concrete recommendations, situational details, or plot/story content) that lack this reassuring/validating conversational form.

title: Empathetic validation and advice-framing
description: This latent fires on the conversational scaffolding of a supportive/therapeutic AI response: short affirming exclamations ('That's great!', 'That's awesome!', 'That's fascinating!'), empathetic reflections that validate the user's feelings or situation ('That sounds really tough', 'That takes courage'), clarifying follow-up questions probing the user's experience, and transitional phrases that set up structured advice or lists ('Here are some suggestions:', 'Before you do anything, ask yourself:', numbered list markers like '1.', '2. **'). It captures the rhetorical moves of acknowledging, praising, or gently probing a person's emotional disclosure before pivoting to guidance. It does NOT include purely factual or narrative content stated without this validating/coaching framing (e.g. plain descriptions of events, technical facts, or list items themselves once the advice content begins), nor does it include neutral third-person exposition unconnected to a supportive dialogue context.
